raw_segments.text: As he spoke, he took up the shield of his son Thrasimes that was lying in his tent,
all gleaming with bronze, for Thrasimes had taken his father's shield.
He grasped his redoubtable, bronze-shod spear, and as soon as he was outside saw the disastrous
rout of the Achaeans who, now that their wall was overthrown, were flying Pelmel before the
As when there is a heavy swell upon the sea, but the waves are dumb, they keep their eyes
on the watch for the quarter whence the fierce winds may spring upon them, but they stay
where they are and set neither this way nor that, till some particular wind sweeps down
from heaven to determine them, even so did the old man ponder whether to make for the
crowd of Danons or go in search of Agamemnon.
In the end he deemed it best to go to the son of Atreus, but meanwhile the hosts were
fighting and killing one another, and the hard bronze rattled on their bodies as they
thrust at one another with their swords and spears.
